label: Adapted Fanonian anti-colonial critique to Pacific and Hawaiian sovereignty
description: In From a Native Daughter, Trask mobilized Fanon’s diagnosis of settler colonialism and native intellectuals to expose U.S. militarism and tourism in Hawaiʻi.
dialecticalTension: Extends anti-colonial liberation philosophy into Oceania.

label: Shared critique of settler-colonial anthropology and tribal/national sovereignty
description: Echoing Deloria’s Custer Died for Your Sins, Trask mounted a fierce philosophical critique of Western historians and anthropologists claiming authority over Native peoples.
dialecticalTension: Unites Continental Native American and Kanaka Maoli critiques of epistemic extraction.

label: Catalyzed Polynesian-Māori critique of imperial research and historiography
description: Trask’s confrontation with settler scholarship in Hawaiʻi directly resonated with Māori philosopher Linda Tuhiwai Smith’s Decolonizing Methodologies.
